knowledge: Rate definitions: the excellence rate is the number of test takers with SAT total >= 1500 divided by the number of test takers; the eligible free rate for K-12 is the K-12 free meal count divided by the K-12 enrollment; the eligible FRPM rate for K-12 is the K-12 FRPM count divided by the K-12 enrollment; the same rates for students aged 5-17 use the corresponding 5-17 counts and enrollment.

Enrollment readings: K-12 means grades 1 through 12; a school's total enrollment is the K-12 enrollment plus the ages 5-17 enrollment; comparing the two bands (how much K-12 exceeds ages 5-17, or their difference) is a subtraction of the two enrollment figures.
Address readings: a school's complete communication address is its street, city, state and zip; "postal street" and "mailing street" are synonyms.

Date readings: "between 1/1/1980 and 12/31/1980" means the year 1980; "between 2009 and 2010" spans 1/1/2009 to 12/31/2010 (both ends included); a "monthly average" is the count over the period divided by 12.

School-type names map onto the code columns: State Special School(s) is the DOC code 31 (or education option code SSS); Elementary School District is DOC 52; Unified School District is DOC 54; Intermediate/Middle School is SOC 62; "exclusively virtual" or "does not offer a physical building" is Virtual = F; a non-chartered school has Charter = 0; "offers a magnet program" means Magnet = 1; "Multiple Provision Types" is a value of the NSLP provision status.

Aggregation readings: "the average of the average math scores" averages each school's average first and then averages those school averages; "schools in Riverside" matches the district name beginning with Riverside; "the highest longitude" means the maximum absolute longitude value.
